not_repaired_deliberately.finding: Trust boundary: an actor able to append arbitrary fabric.spine.result receipts could fabricate a certification.
not_repaired_deliberately.why: that is the product's existing ledger-authoritative trust model, not a property this lane introduces or may change; the re-derivation still validates the observation against the filesystem.

repaired_findings.finding: F2 (verified): a verifier session re-deriving against a NEW receipt under the same run identity raised EventConflict on the observation record — the R7 failure class at a different seam.
repaired_findings.fix: the fabric.canonical_verification_observed idempotency key now covers the whole observation payload, so identical re-delivery dedupes and a new re-derivation records a new observation (the product's established B6 pattern in control/action_envelope.py).

repaired_findings.finding: F3/F4 (code-level): the subject guard only compared keys present on both sides, and blank refs disabled divergence detection, so a receipt naming another subject under a different key could be certified.
repaired_findings.fix: the policy moved to _subject_diverges: a declared subject the observation does not name — or names blank — is a divergence and the session declines.

repaired_findings.finding: F5 (defensive depth): the acceptance rule accepted any non-None marker value.
repaired_findings.fix: only the one marker jarvis_foundry.fabric.model defines satisfies the rule; anything else is refused by name.

F2 robustness (extra probe p6b): canonical_verifier_dispatch appends fabric.canonical_verification_observed under idempotency key 'fabric.canonical_verification_observed:{run_id}:{verdict}'. After a successful certification, a NEW fabric.spine.result receipt (different receipt_id/effect_id) plus a re-dispatch of the SAME run_id re-derived MATCH and raised EventConflict('idempotency conflict for fabric.canonical_verification_observed:adv-run-subject-a:MATCH') out of the helper - observed escaping canonical_verifier_dispatch. The R7 catch in mission/loop.py wraps only capture_binding, so this seam is not converted there. No false PASS results: the original observation is preserved and the duplicate append is refused. Production reachability not established (builder attempts mint new run ids f'{run_id}-verify'; verifier-reuse logic exists at mission/loop.py:1928).

F3 subject guard is key-shape dependent (code-level): the declared-vs-claimed divergence check compares only keys present in BOTH sides (_SPINE_SUBJECT_KEYS = path/target/source_ref/worktree). For the materialized hash mission both sides use 'path', and divergence IS declined (p5: declared .../evidence.bin vs receipt .../other.bin -> dispatch None, no observation recorded; positive control with the declared subject IS certified). Residual: if a contract's declared JSON names the subject under a different key than the receipt's observed, no comparison happens, and for hash.file.sha256 the verifier re-derives from claimed['path'], so certification would follow the receipt's own path. NOT exercised end-to-end (needs a contract whose declared payload uses another key).

F4 blank refs disable divergence detection (code-level): _same_subject returns True when either side is blank. For hash.file.sha256 an absent claimed path fails closed (KeyError -> UNKNOWN -> decline), but verifiers that default a missing path to owned_root (e.g. dir.list uses Path(claimed.get('path') or owned_root)) could verify the root instead of the declared subject. Not demonstrated end-to-end.

F5 defensive depth (code-level): MissionLoop._pass_requires_jarvis_predicate returns None immediately for ANY non-None jarvis_predicate without re-checking the value against CANONICAL_PREDICATE_EVIDENCE; the single production call site (mission/loop.py:2248-2251) passes only _jarvis_predicate_satisfied() output (the constant or None), verified by grep.

F6 semantics: when the canonical predicate is present, the acceptance rule skips the path-shaped artifact checks entirely (including declared expected_artifacts beyond the certified action subject). This is the documented intent ('stronger artifact predicate'); no false success demonstrated.

repairs: R6 verifier routing: the mission verifier step for a step whose contract capability resolves to a Fabric action kind is answered by the canonical JARVIS predicate over the recorded receipt (fabric/adapter.py canonical_verifier_dispatch + fabric/loop.py canonical_predicate_verdict), and the acceptance rule 'Model PASS is insufficient: JARVIS must see an artifact predicate' accepts that re-derived predicate as the predicate (mission/loop.py).
R7 binding drift: a pass resumed after the frozen binding drifted is refused honestly (BLOCKED with the ledger's own reason) instead of propagating the ledger's EventConflict out of the loop.

repairs.R6: Mission verifier routing for deterministic local actions: a verifier session on a step whose contract capability resolves to a Fabric action kind is answered by re-running the canonical JARVIS predicate over the step's recorded receipt; the verdict is re-derived from reality, never trusted from the recorded claim, and the acceptance rule that demands a JARVIS-owned artifact predicate is satisfied by that re-derivation instead of by a path heuristic.
repairs.R7: Binding drift on a resumed verification pass: the verdict identity is derived from the pass contract, so a pass resumed after the frozen state drifted cannot re-freeze a different binding under the same identity.  The ledger refused it with EventConflict, which escaped the mission loop; the loop now refuses honestly (BLOCKED with the ledger's reason) and leaves the resume to a fresh attempt.
